claim: Defines a single-agent trajectory P of length m as a sequence of d-dimensional feature vectors (e.g. a player or ball coordinate over time); an agent is a dynamic object of interest such as a player or the ball.
Defines a multi-agent trajectory P_K with K agents (a team, both teams, or players plus the ball) as a sequence of per-time-step features.
Defines the per-time-step feature of a multi-agent trajectory as the stacked K-by-d matrix of all K agents' features at time i.
Defines a relation sequence R_K as the length-m sequence of K-by-K relation matrices between agents over time.
Defines each pairwise relation entry R_{i,k,l} at time i as a function h (e.g. a distance function or a Gaussian kernel) of the two agents' features.
